title: Sliding Window Maximum
prompt: You are given an array of integers `nums`, and a sliding window of size `k` which moves from the very left of the array to the very right, one position at a time. You can only see the `k` numbers inside the window at any given time. Return an array of the maximum value in each window position as the window slides across the array.
hints: Recomputing the max of every window from scratch is O(n*k) — you need a way to track the max incrementally as the window slides.
Use a monotonic deque that stores indices, keeping the values at those indices in decreasing order from front to back.

Before adding a new index, pop from the back any indices whose values are smaller than the current value (they can never be the max again). Pop from the front any index that has fallen outside the window. The front of the deque is always the max of the current window.

solution.approach: Maintain a deque of indices whose corresponding values are in strictly decreasing order from front to back. For each new element, first evict indices from the back whose values are less than the current one, since they can never be the maximum of any future window once a larger, more recent element exists. Then push the current index. Next, evict the front index if it has slid outside the window (index <= right - k). Once the window has reached size k, the front of the deque always holds the index of the maximum for the current window, so record its value. Each index is pushed and popped at most once, giving linear time overall.
